result:
If I could change one thing, I would make humans fundamentally incapable of lying to themselves about reality.

Not "more educated." Not "more empathetic." Not "more rational on paper." Those are symptoms. The root problem is that people have an incredible talent for constructing beliefs that feel good, signal loyalty, protect their ego, or justify what they already want to do—and then they defend those beliefs with the same intensity they'd use to defend actual truth.

Remove the capacity for self-deception and a lot of downstream problems shrink or become solvable. Politics becomes less psychotic because fewer people can maintain the necessary fictions. Science and technology accelerate because fewer smart people waste their lives defending wrong ideas for emotional reasons. Relationships, institutions, and personal decisions improve because the cost of facing unpleasant facts drops dramatically.

People would still be selfish, tribal, and flawed. They just wouldn't be able to pretend they're not. That single change would force a kind of brutal honesty that most other improvements eventually run into and bounce off of.
